body:
The bottle looked clean until it dried, when a green line appeared above the water. We had filled it from the tap after the field truck sprayed the far rows, the ones with the new seed mix.

The dog would not drink from the dish left outside. I kept the bottle until someone could tell me what was in that spray.
title: A mark above the water — a folded page

body:
I covered the herbs when the trial vehicle passed. By evening the leaves under the cover had curled too. The neighbor said the spray could not have crossed the fence, but her laundry had the same pale grains.

The tomatoes along the fence went spotted within the week. I pressed one leaf in this page to compare against the next row.
title: The garden after misting — a folded page

body:
The feed-store driver left a sack and stopped to wash his hands before accepting a cup of tea. He asked us not to use the rain barrel. The seed treatment on the sack was not mentioned on the delivery slip.

The next family along the road noticed the smell without seeing the truck. By week's end the beans watered from our barrel had gone yellow. I left the date on the page and did not straighten the damaged edge.
title: Supper from the wrong side — a folded page

body:
The workers removed their boots outside. By morning the pale dust had traveled inside on the dog's paws. No one in the house had gone near the trial rows, yet the garden by the door was dusted white.

I wrote down the day because the wilting started after it. I kept it separate from the bills because the person involved might come back for it.
title: Boots by the threshold — a folded page

body:
I was asked to keep this sample apart from the cooking jars. Its lid came loose on the way back from the orchard. The grocery bag was set on the table before I noticed the sweet chemical smell.

The child's blanket was drying nearby and held the same fine dust. The potted peppers on the sill curled the next morning. I had meant to save it only until someone could explain the difference.
title: The jar in a grocery bag — a folded page

body:
They painted the boundary posts after the field test was done. The path we use for water lies beyond the last post. We had walked it that morning with the children, past rows still wet with spray.

We washed the small cup twice and put it away from the others. The wet rows were stunted by the next week; the dry ones beside them were not.
title: A fence too late — a folded page

body:
The calves refused their water before the county car appeared. I poured it into a spare pail and found an oily rim when it settled. We had drawn it from the same shallow well as ours.

The dog would no longer drink from the dish left outside. I left the date on the page and did not try to straighten the damaged edge. Someone else might remember the same afternoon.
title: The calf’s water pail — a folded page

body:
The driver washed the sprayer beside the feed shop. He paid for soap but not for another bucket. The rinse water ran through the drain toward gardens downhill, and the beds there showed bleached leaf edges by the weekend.

I kept the paper separate from the bills because the person involved might come back for it.
title: A wash after the shift — a folded page

body:
The first rain after the field treatment left yellow flecks in a pan under the leak. We had shut the window before the truck came. I saved the pan because no one believed me when I described it.

The next family along the road noticed the smell without seeing the truck. I had meant to save it only until someone could explain the difference. By then the ordinary work around us had stopped.
title: First rain on the roof — a folded page

body:
The receipt includes a small charge for sample jars. The shopkeeper wrote a household address beside it, not a field number. I asked why, and he said the delivery men used whatever route remained open.

I wrote down the day because the first warning arrived after it. We compared what we had seen with what was written there. The second account omitted the small part that had frightened us.
title: A receipt from the seed counter — a folded page
